title: Fall back to hyprsunset gamma on displays without DDC/CI
head: a17fd97e64f2
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A malformed brightness step poisons a healthy monitor's DDC cache and routes later valid steps through global gamma
leads.consequence: On a working DP-1 DDC monitor, `omarchy-brightness-display --monitor DP-1 bad` makes the DDC helper return 1 for an unrecognized step. The wrapper mistakes this for absent DDC, writes a 60-second marker and then returns 1 from its own gamma parser. A following valid `--monitor DP-1 50%` skips DDC and instead dims every output via hyprsunset. Status reads also return gamma rather than actual DDC brightness until the marker expires. Validate syntax before inferring DDC failure, or distinguish unsupported step from DDC transport failure.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; Opus F2 S3 typo case, sandbox-reproduced.

leads.summary: PR #13261's existing internal-panel gamma range resets or kills this PR's fallback when both features are preserved
leads.consequence: Open PR #13261 also changes this exact script and introduces a gamma helper. On manually reconciling both overlapping branches while retaining both features, setting ordinary internal-panel brightness calls `gamma_command set 100`; its helper can additionally kill the hyprsunset it started at neutral gamma. Therefore an external no-DDC display dimmed by this PR to 20-50% jumps back to full whenever an internal display is adjusted, while this PR's 60-second no-DDC marker remains. This is a semantic conflict in addition to the overlapping hunks, not just textual overlap. Coordinate a single gamma owner/range and preserve external dimming on internal adjustments.
leads.triage: verified_factual_published; Coordinator read #13261 patch (gamma_command set 100 on internal steps; gamma_command closes lock_fd); Opus self-check reconfirmed at fd986e12.

leads.summary: PR #13286 replaces the entire modified entrypoint, so merging its implementation discards this PR's fallback
leads.consequence: Open PR #13286 replaces the whole shell implementation with `exec omarchy-media brightness display "$@"`. The gamma fallback and DDC-negative marker added here live only in the removed shell body. A merge resolved by taking #13286's entrypoint loses the fallback altogether, while resolving in favor of this PR loses the new native command. Port this fallback to omarchy-media or coordinate the two PRs before merging either.
leads.triage: verified_factual_published; Draft PR body becomes exec omarchy-media; Opus confirmed omarchy-media has no gamma code.

leads.summary: PR #9876's verified-write failure becomes a gamma fallback and its expected failure test fails if both changes land
leads.consequence: Open PR #9876 changes the DDC helper to verify writes, and its test requires `DDC_WRITE_FAIL=1 ... 45%` to exit nonzero, leave the external monitor readable and keep its bus. With this wrapper, that failed write triggers `mark_ddc_missing`, sends 45% to global gamma, prints 45 and returns success instead; subsequent reads skip DDC for 60 seconds. The #9876 test's explicit failed-write assertion fails after a combined merge, and a transient verified-write failure dims every output while hiding a working monitor. Distinguish failed writes from unsupported monitor detection.
leads.triage: verified_factual_published; Coordinator read #9876 test; Opus self-check added that reads within 60 s would also come from gamma.

leads.summary: Gamma setter reports success and OSD brightness when hyprsunset IPC is unavailable
leads.consequence: When `uwsm-app` fails to start hyprsunset, or the daemon/socket never becomes available, all five `hyprctl hyprsunset gamma N` calls can fail. The code discards their exit statuses, `gamma_brightness` turns any failed read into 100, then unconditionally prints N and returns success. The slider or OSD claims it set N while the image stays unchanged; the no-DDC marker prevents a fresh DDC probe meanwhile. Existing test's `pgrep` stub always returns 0 and `hyprctl` setter always succeeds, so it cannot catch this. Check success/readback and propagate failure rather than printing a target that did not stick.
leads.triage: opus_followup_confirmed_published; opus/followup-1.md Q2, run review4; published as smaller note.

leads.summary: Absolute step with leading-zero octal-invalid digits can bypass the 20% gamma floor
leads.consequence: For a no-DDC external monitor, an accepted `08%` step assigns the string `08` to target. Bash arithmetic interprets a leading zero as octal; both `(( target < gamma_min ))` and `(( target > 100 ))` reject 08 rather than applying the clamp. The script still sends `hyprctl hyprsunset gamma 08`; hyprsunset uses `std::stof` (decimal 8), making the output 8% and the screen harder to see despite the stated 20% safety floor. Convert user digits explicitly in base 10 before arithmetic and add a leading-zero test.
leads.triage: opus_followup_confirmed_published; opus/followup-1.md Q1; CLI/custom-binding only, low impact; published as smaller note.

leads.summary: Time-profile transitions in hyprsunset reset the fallback gamma without invalidating this PR's cache or restoring brightness
leads.consequence: When a user follows Omarchy's documented multi-profile nightlight schedule and a profile changes while an external no-DDC monitor is dimmed, hyprsunset's scheduler assigns `GAMMA = newProfile.gamma` (default 100%). This PR does not observe profile changes, so the monitor abruptly returns to full brightness despite a still-live failed-DDC marker; another brightness invocation is needed to restore dimming. It is not caused by the nightlight temperature toggle alone, which only sets temperature.
leads.triage: partly_in_opus_final; Opus covered default profile 07:00 re-apply; mentioned in the gamma-outlives note. Multi-profile variant not published separately.

leads.summary: A hyprsunset running in a different compositor session suppresses startup for the target session
leads.consequence: With two Hyprland sessions for one user, `pgrep -x hyprsunset` may match the daemon in the other session although hyprsunset IPC is per `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE`. This script skips startup for the current compositor; `hyprctl hyprsunset gamma N` then cannot reach its instance and H5's false-success behaviour follows. Probe the socket for the active compositor, not an arbitrary process name.
leads.triage: dropped; Multi-session edge case; not verified, low value.

leads.summary: An absent focused-monitor name in a monitor JSON response is mistaken for a named external display
leads.consequence: If `hyprctl monitors -j` yields an object with `focused:true` but no `name` (malformed or incomplete response), `jq -r '.[] | select(.focused == true).name'` outputs literal `null`. The wrapper treats `null` as a nonempty external monitor, marks DDC unavailable, and a subsequent brightness key sets global gamma rather than selecting the internal backlight. For an entirely absent focused object jq outputs empty and the old backlight path is used, so distinguish absent field from empty result. Reject literal null/nonexistent monitor identifiers before selecting DDC or gamma.
leads.triage: dropped; Requires malformed hyprctl output; pre-existing selection code.

limits: Source-only boundary hunt. No PR scripts or tests were executed, and no live compositor, DDC hardware or UI was queried. Behaviour requiring actual display calibration or hardware-specific DDC errors remains unobserved.

Related open-PR consequences are derived from the pinned heads of their source/test files, not from constructing a resolved combined merge; maintainers must resolve overlapping hunks to retain all behaviours.

No PKGBUILD exists in this Omarchy tree. Hyprsunset 0.4.0-3 was identified via public Arch package metadata; upstream hyprsunset v0.4.0 source was fetched read-only. Hyprland hyprctl and uwsm-app upstream sources were not fetched, so no assertion here depends on undocumented details of their command-line parsing.

flags.claim: The panel keeps showing the value it tried to set.
flags.why: Only until the panel's next refresh. While the panel is open it re-reads every 5 s (Panel.qml:379-384 Timer 5000 -> refresh -> omarchy-monitor-state), and the no-argument read path does not take the lock, so the slider snaps back to the real (unchanged) gamma within 5 s, or on the next open. My final.md made the same overstatement and contradicted its own interaction note about the 5 s poll.

flags.claim: Table row 'one transient getvcp failure, then 5%-': Base 'exit 1, nothing changes'.
flags.why: In the run the getvcp failure happened inside the 5%- press itself (S2: ddc-fail-once armed, then step1 = 5%-). The base exits 1 only for that press. If the failure came first, in a separate call (for example a panel read), the base would simply retry on the 5%- and succeed over DDC. The head column is right either way.

flags.claim: ...so each of these marks a working DDC monitor as DDC-less for 60 s and applies the step to gamma instead.
flags.why: For an unrecognised step the step itself is not applied. set_gamma_brightness returns 1 (:85-86), so the script exits 1 and only the following valid steps within 60 s go to gamma (S3 head step1 rc=1 with gamma untouched; step2 50% -> gamma 50). A failed read (:108-109) has no step: the read returns gamma. The table row for the typo is correct. My final.md F2 prose had the same overstatement.

flags.claim: of ten single-line mutations of the new logic, the updated test caught only the removal of the 20% floor.
flags.why: Nine mutants (M1-M9) target the PR's new code in bin/omarchy-brightness-display. M10 targets the DDC helper, which the PR does not change, and is reported separately in the same paragraph ('The base test's check ... was also lost'). M1-M9 each change one line; M10 replaces a three-line block. 'Caught only the floor' is correct (M2 only). My final.md used the same 'ten single-line ... new logic' wording.

flags.claim: when hyprsunset cannot start or its IPC does not answer ... about 2 s when the launch fails ..., about 1 s when hyprsunset runs but does not answer.
flags.why: (a) What was tested is hyprctl being unable to connect (exit 3). A hyprsunset that accepts the connection but never replies would instead block the press indefinitely: hyprctl's hyprsunset path does a blocking read with no timeout (requestIPC, hyprctl main.cpp:283-333), unlike the 5 s SO_RCVTIMEO on Hyprland's socket (main.cpp:209-213). That is a hypothesis, not run. (b) The times apply to targets below 100. Targets of 100 (`+5%` from the fallback, `100%`) return after about 1.0 s with the launch and about 13 ms without it, because the fallback read already equals 100.

flags.claim: Checking the read-back after the loop and returning 1 when it never matches would surface this.
flags.why: Only partly. When hyprsunset is unreachable, the fallback read of 100 still matches a target of 100, so that case stays silent. The check would also report failure for sets that worked: `0100%` (sends 0100, reads 100; run4 Q1) and, under comma-decimal locales, 53 (reads 52; run3 S6.de.read53). The check needs the locale fix and a normalised target, or a test of hyprctl's exit status and reply format, to be reliable.

flags.claim: Internal, Apple and working-DDC paths are unchanged.
flags.why: The source of the internal and Apple branches is unchanged, and the DDC branch is unchanged when the helper succeeds. But the DDC branch's failure handling changed (the draft's own second section), and the lock leak blocks all three branches (first section). The sentence is framed by 'on the happy path', so this is minor.

Minor. setsid also calls setsid() and forks first when the caller leads its process group (setsid.c:98-123); the relevant point is that it closes no descriptors. uwsm-app gets `exec systemd-run --user --scope ...` only with the default scope unit type (uwsm main.py:2081-2091,3731-3733). With UWSM_APP_UNIT_TYPE=service the manager spawns the process, which does not inherit the descriptor. Omarchy does not set that variable.

flags.claim: ran in an isolated sandbox with every external command stubbed
flags.why: Minor. Stubs covered hyprctl, pgrep, setsid (as a wrapper), uwsm-app, hyprsunset, ddcutil, brightnessctl, omarchy-osd, omarchy-hw-display and the two monitor helpers. Basic utilities (bash, flock, date, awk, mkdir, sleep, grep) ran for real inside the sandbox.

Correct for absolute steps, but part of the finding and fix is dropped. Leading-zero relative steps `+08%`/`08%-` also hit the octal error and jump to 20% whatever the current value (run4 Q1), so :82 and :84 need `10#` too. On a DDC-capable monitor `08%` now ends at gamma 8 plus the 60 s marker (run4 Q1b). Optional to include.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** on the happy path the fallback does what the description says. When the DDC probe fails on an external display, steps go to `hyprctl hyprsunset gamma`, are clamped to 20..100, the failed probe is remembered for 60 s, and reads return the gamma value so the Display panel gets a slider. The internal and Apple branches, and DDC steps that succeed, behave as before. The updated test passes on this head and fails against the base script.

Two behavioural problems showed up in sandboxed runs with stubbed `hyprctl`, `ddcutil`, `uwsm-app` and `hyprsunset`.

### Starting hyprsunset from this script keeps the brightness lock held

`set_gamma_brightness` starts hyprsunset (`bin/omarchy-brightness-display:76`) while the script holds `flock` on `omarchy-brightness-display.lock` (`:136-137`). Only stdout and stderr are redirected, so the daemon inherits the lock descriptor. Nothing in the real launch chain closes it: util-linux `setsid` closes no descriptors before `execvp`, `uwsm-app` with its default unit type (Omarchy does not set `UWSM_APP_UNIT_TYPE`) execs `systemd-run --user --scope`, and that `execvpe`s hyprsunset in place (per upstream source; this chain was not executed). A `flock` lock belongs to the open file, so it stays held for as long as hyprsunset runs.

```text
hyprsunset not running (default: Omarchy does not autostart it)
  step 1  --monitor DP-2 5%-   -> starts hyprsunset, gamma 95, OSD 95
          hyprsunset now holds fd -> omarchy-brightness-display.lock
  step 2  --monitor DP-2 5%-   -> flock -n fails, exit 0, no calls, gamma still 95
  step 3  --monitor eDP-1 +5%  -> flock -n fails, laptop backlight unchanged
  kill hyprsunset              -> lock free, steps work again
```

Controls: with hyprsunset already running (as after the nightlight toggle), repeated steps work. Adding `{lock_fd}>&-` to the launch line also makes repeated steps work.

**Impact:** on a session where hyprsunset is not already running, the first gamma step works, then the brightness keys and the Display panel slider silently stop for every display (laptop panel, Apple and DDC monitors included) until hyprsunset exits. The panel shows the value it tried to set until its next refresh (within 5 s while open).

**Suggested change:** close the descriptor for the launch, for example `setsid uwsm-app -- hyprsunset {lock_fd}>&- >/dev/null 2>&1 &`, or start hyprsunset before taking the lock. A test with `pgrep` reporting "not running" would cover the launch path, which the current `pgrep` mock (always succeeds) skips.

### Any DDC helper failure switches a working DDC monitor to global gamma, and the dimming stays

`:148` (step) and `:108-109` (read) call `mark_ddc_missing` whenever `omarchy-brightness-display-ddc` exits nonzero. The helper also exits 1 for a transient `getvcp` failure, a failed `setvcp` and an unrecognised step, so each of these marks a working DDC monitor as DDC-less for 60 s. A failed step then goes to gamma instead (a typo step still exits 1), and later steps and reads use gamma until the marker expires. The base treated transient read failures as retryable on the next call without caching them, and its test asserted that; the updated test deletes the marker by hand before checking the retry (`test/shell.d/brightness-display-test.sh:140`).

| DDC monitor DP-1, sandbox run | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `5%-` whose `getvcp` fails once | exit 1, nothing changes | gamma 95 (all outputs), marker written |
| next `5%-` | DDC `setvcp` (45%) | gamma 90, no DDC call |
| after 60 s, `+5%` | DDC | DDC `setvcp` (55%), **gamma stays 90** |
| typo `50`, then `50%` | `50%` goes to DDC | typo writes the marker, `50%` sets gamma 50 |
| one failed `setvcp`, `30%` | exit 1 | gamma 30 |

**Impact:** on a monitor where DDC works, one failed DDC call turns the keys and slider into global gamma for 60 s, which also dims every other output. Dimming set in that window survives the return to DDC control: reads then report the DDC value, and nothing in the brightness UI brings gamma back to 100. How often real monitors produce such failures was not measured.

**Suggested change:** mark a display as DDC-less only when the read probe fails, not on invalid arguments or failed writes (consider requiring more than one failed probe for a monitor that has answered before). When DDC control succeeds while gamma is below 100, restore gamma.

### Related open PRs

- #13261 also adds hyprsunset gamma to this script, for the internal panel below 1%. Its internal-panel steps call `gamma_command set 100`, so if both features are kept, adjusting the laptop panel would undo this PR's external dimming. It already launches its gamma helper with `{lock_fd}>&-`.
- #13286 (draft) replaces the body of `bin/omarchy-brightness-display` with `exec omarchy-media brightness display "$@"`, which has no gamma fallback.
- #9876 makes DDC writes verify and adds a test that a rejected write exits nonzero and leaves the monitor readable over DDC. With this PR's wrapper, that rejected write would go to gamma and exit 0 instead, and reads for the next 60 s would come from gamma.

### Smaller notes

- **Gamma outlives the display it was set for:** after dimming the TV to 20%, `--monitor eDP-1 100%` sets the laptop backlight and leaves gamma at 20. After unplugging the TV, the laptop stays dimmed and its brightness keys cannot fix it. This goes a step beyond the acknowledged "dims any other screen" limit; a restart of hyprsunset or the default profile's daily 07:00 re-apply resets it.
- **A failed gamma set still reports success:** when hyprsunset cannot start or `hyprctl` cannot connect to it, every read falls back to 100, the sets fail silently, and `set_gamma_brightness` still prints the target and exits 0. The OSD shows, for example, 95 on every `5%-` press while nothing changes, and each press below 100% takes about 2 s when the launch fails (`sleep 1` plus the retry loop), about 1 s when hyprsunset runs but cannot be reached. Checking whether any set command succeeded, rather than only the read-back (a target of 100 matches the fallback reading), would surface this.
- **Leading-zero absolute steps skip the floor:** for `08%`, bash arithmetic treats `08` as invalid octal, so both clamp checks fail with an error and neither applies. `hyprctl hyprsunset gamma 08` is sent, and hyprsunset parses it as 8. Only manual CLI use or custom bindings can produce such a step (keys and the Display panel send plain integers). `$((10#${BASH_REMATCH[1]}))` in all three step branches avoids it (the relative forms `+08%` and `08%-` also misbehave and land on 20%).
- **Comma-decimal locales:** hyprsunset replies with a dot (`95.000000`). Under `de_DE.UTF-8`, bash `printf '%.0f'` in `gamma_brightness` prints an "invalid number" error and returns 1, so a read exits 1. Some replies are not integral (target 53 comes back as `52.999996`), so 53 reads as 52 and setting it takes 5 calls. `LC_ALL=C printf '%.0f'` avoids this.

**Optional test improvement:** of nine single-line mutations of the new logic, the updated test caught only the removal of the 20% floor. Not caught: the 60 s marker never honoured or never written (the DDC-less mock has no I2C bus, so the DDC helper's own cache hides it; the author's bus-found, `getvcp`-fails case is only tested after deleting the marker by hand), an integer-only reply regex (the mock replies `50`, real hyprsunset `50.000000`), no hyprsunset launch, no retry loop, `N%-` adding instead of subtracting, and no upper clamp. The base test's check of the DDC helper's own "unavailable" cache was also lost. A bus-found mock, `%f` replies and `pgrep` returning "not running" would cover most of these.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the pinned head and merge-base, and of hyprsunset 0.4.0, hyprctl (Hyprland 0.56.2), uwsm 0.27.0, systemd-run 262 and util-linux setsid 2.42.4 source. The PR's test and scenario scripts ran in an isolated sandbox with every display, DDC and hyprsunset command stubbed; the `setsid` stub ran the real util-linux `setsid`. No display, DDC hardware, real hyprsunset or live Hyprland session was used, and the real `uwsm-app` / `systemd-run --scope` launch chain was not executed. Related open PRs were compared from their current heads, not merged.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
